# awscc_mediaconnect_source_endpoint (Data Source)

Data Source schema for AWS::MediaConnect::SourceEndpoint



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `id` (String) Uniquely identifies the resource.

### Read-Only

- `arn` (String)
- `associated_resource_details` (Attributes) The details of the resource that is associated with a source endpoint. This is a union type, so exactly one of its members is set, depending on the type of the source endpoint. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--associated_resource_details))
- `availability_zone` (String) The Availability Zone in which the source endpoint is located.
- `availability_zone_id` (String) The ID of the Availability Zone in which the source endpoint is located.
- `configuration` (Attributes) The configuration settings for a source endpoint. This is a union type, so exactly one of its members is set, depending on the type of the source endpoint. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--configuration))
- `connection_state` (String)
- `created_at` (String) The date and time when the source endpoint was created.
- `description` (String) The description of the source endpoint.
- `lifecycle_management` (String)
- `name` (String) The name of the source endpoint.
- `region_name` (String) The name of the Amazon Web Services Region in which the source endpoint is located.
- `registration_state` (String)
- `source_endpoint_id` (String) The unique identifier of the source endpoint.
- `source_type` (String)
- `tags` (Attributes List) The tags associated with the source endpoint. Each tag is a key-value pair. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tags))
- `updated_at` (String) The date and time when the source endpoint was last updated.

### Nested Schema for `configuration.standard.protocol_configuration`

Read-Only:

- `rist` (Attributes) The configuration settings for a source endpoint that uses the RIST protocol. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--configuration--standard--protocol_configuration--rist))
- `rtp` (Attributes) The configuration settings for a source endpoint that uses the RTP protocol. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--configuration--standard--protocol_configuration--rtp))

<a id="nestedatt--configuration--standard--protocol_configuration--rist"></a>
### Nested Schema for `configuration.standard.protocol_configuration.rist`

Read-Only:

- `destination_ingest_port` (Number) The port on the destination that receives the content. The valid range is 3000 to 30000.
- `recovery_latency_milliseconds` (Number) The amount of time, in milliseconds, that the source endpoint allows for recovering lost packets. The valid range is 10 to 10000.


<a id="nestedatt--configuration--standard--protocol_configuration--rtp"></a>
### Nested Schema for `configuration.standard.protocol_configuration.rtp`

Read-Only:

- `destination_ingest_port` (Number) The port on the destination that receives the content. The valid range is 3000 to 30000.
- `forward_error_correction_state` (String)


<a id="nestedatt--configuration--standard--protocol_configuration--srt_caller"></a>
### Nested Schema for `configuration.standard.protocol_configuration.srt_caller`

Read-Only:

- `destination_ingest_port` (Number) The port on which the destination listens for the connection. The valid range is 3000 to 30000.
- `encryption_passphrase` (Attributes) The configuration for the Secrets Manager secret that holds the key or passphrase used to encrypt an endpoint connection. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--configuration--standard--protocol_configuration--srt_caller--encryption_passphrase))
- `minimum_latency_milliseconds` (Number) The minimum latency, in milliseconds, for the SRT connection. The valid range is 10 to 10000.

<a id="nestedatt--configuration--standard--protocol_configuration--srt_caller--encryption_passphrase"></a>
### Nested Schema for `configuration.standard.protocol_configuration.srt_caller.encryption_passphrase`

Read-Only:

- `secret_arn` (String) The ARN of the Secrets Manager secret that holds the key or passphrase. The secret must be encrypted with a customer managed Amazon Web Services KMS key that is enabled and symmetric; it cannot use the Amazon Web Services managed key aws/secretsmanager. The secret must be in the same Amazon Web Services account and Region as the endpoint.



<a id="nestedatt--configuration--standard--protocol_configuration--srt_listener"></a>
### Nested Schema for `configuration.standard.protocol_configuration.srt_listener`

Read-Only:

- `encryption_passphrase` (Attributes) The configuration for the Secrets Manager secret that holds the key or passphrase used to encrypt an endpoint connection. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--configuration--standard--protocol_configuration--srt_listener--encryption_passphrase))
- `minimum_latency_milliseconds` (Number) The minimum latency, in milliseconds, for the SRT connection. The valid range is 10 to 10000.
- `source_address` (String) The IP address that the source endpoint listens on for incoming connections.
- `source_listener_port` (Number) The port that the source endpoint listens on for incoming connections. The valid range is 1024 to 65535.
- `stream_id` (String) The stream ID that identifies the content for the SRT connection.

<a id="nestedatt--configuration--standard--protocol_configuration--srt_listener--encryption_passphrase"></a>

Read-Only:

- `secret_arn` (String) The ARN of the Secrets Manager secret that holds the key or passphrase. The secret must be encrypted with a customer managed Amazon Web Services KMS key that is enabled and symmetric; it cannot use the Amazon Web Services managed key aws/secretsmanager. The secret must be in the same Amazon Web Services account and Region as the endpoint.
